title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents

evidence.label: 明确提出新的评测资料或框架
evidence.excerpt: Motivated by these gaps, we propose a new evaluation suite that combines utility of user simulators for evaluating agents and two measures of fidelity to real users: population-level fidelity assesses collective interaction patterns, while trace-level fidelity assesses the preservation of individual users' goals, constraints, and persona.

evidence.label: 描述任务、问题或评测环境
evidence.excerpt: Evaluating six user simulators on 351 real multi-turn sessions in which 348 distinct users across 23 languages and agents work together to create and refine artifacts such as full-stack web apps, games, design assets, and automated workflows, we find that population-level measures can miss when a simulated user pursues the wrong goal, ignores a constraint, or behaves out of character, highlighting the need to assess fidelity at comprehensive granularities.

evidence.label: 描述评分指标或评测协议
evidence.excerpt: To understand what a high benchmark score tells us about simulator quality, we (meta-)evaluate the metrics themselves.
